To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Sakaigawamassive, the oldest unit of the Hida-Ohi terrane, is a Permian magmatite, which was metamorphosed at high-P/T conditions in the Late Permian to Early Triassic and was then accreted to the proto-Japan island arc system.

the Triassic high-P-T metamorphism in the Sakaigwa unit, Kii peninsula, Japan, is not related to the East Asian continental margins, but to subduction-accretion complexes on the Pacific side, and that the proto-Japan arc system was fringed but not yet attached to the Eurasian continent.

(a) the 40Ar/ 39Ar ages of the Sakaigawe unit are 218.4 ± 0.4,228.8 ± 0.9 and231.9 ± 0.7 Ma (2σ;49–63%39Ar-release), (b) the ages are interpreted as the time of the high-P/T metamorphic event, (c) the event occurred in the proto-Japan arc system and not on the Eurasian continental margin
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible merger of the CAOB with large-scale tetrads of the East Asian continental margins.
the tectonic evolution of the Central Asian orogenic belt in the East Asian region.
the timing of the amalgamation of the Central Asian and Indosinian systems with East Asian continental margin systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a major part of the Central Asian orogenic belt was not part of the East Asian continental crust, but was a Pacific-derived terrane.

the East Asian continental crust was not yet connected to the Central Asian Organic Belt during the Late Permian to Early Triassic, and that the latter system did not reach as far south as the Qinling-Dabe-Sulu belt, but rather extended southwards into Indochina.
the proto-Japan arc was part of the Central Asian Oceanic Belt and that its collision with the proto-Eurasian margin caused the Indosinian orogeny, not the opposite.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Central Asian Organic Belt was a long-lived system that was not restricted to the Asian continent, but extended to the Pacific side of proto-Japan.
the East Asian margin was not a simple plate boundary but a complex system of terranes and subduction–accreting systems.
the proto-Japan terrane was not a fragment of the North China continent, but a fragment of the Pacific Ocean.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Central Asian Organic Belt, which was the site of the largest Phanerozoic orogenic system, was connected to the East Asian continental arc system, and that this connection might have been established as far back as Late Permian times.

the Central Asian Organic Belt was not a single tectonic unit, but a system of terranes, which were assembled in the Permian and Triassic, and that the East Asian continental margins were not a single unit either.

the East Asian margin is a composite of several tectonic elements, including a subduction–collision system, which was active in the Permian to Triassic, and which is not part of the East Asian continental arc system.
